fishingbat: A large fish-eating bat of Central American rivers, in flight low over water, both wings spread wide to either side, seen from the front. The animal is shown entirely on its own, isolated, with no other object of any kind in the picture. ITS HEAD IS A NARROW POINTED BAT'S HEAD, small and furry and TAPERING SMOOTHLY FORWARD TO A NEAT POINTED MUZZLE like a mouse's or a little fox's, with the tip of its nose the narrowest part of its face. The face is SLIM AND WEDGE-SHAPED seen from the front, NARROWER AT THE CHIN THAN BETWEEN THE EARS, with a straight clean profile, a small pointed chin, tidy close-lying fur and no loose hanging skin. Two upright pointed ears stand tall on top of its head and its eyes are small and dark. Its upper lip is divided by one narrow vertical cleft. ITS HIND FEET ARE ENORMOUS, hanging down well below its body on long bare legs and armed with BIG CURVED HOOKED CLAWS for gaffing fish out of the water. Long narrow pointed wings of orange-brown leather, bright rusty-orange fur
